items.title: Chinese memory makers have reportedly stocked up on enough western DUV machines for the next three years of expansion
items.summary: More chips!
items.body: The fact that world powers are engaged in a technological arms race is now pretty common knowledge. AI capabilities are starting to serve as national and international litmus tests for soft and hard power, but these capabilities depend on the physical hardware underneath them. And while China has been lagging behind the West in this regard, it has very quickly been playing catch-up. It's not all as simple as east vs west, however, as much of China's hardware is still, in fact, bought from the Western company ASML. The Financial Times reports that, "according to a person with knowledge of the matter", [Chinese memory makers] CXMT and YMTC have managed to stock up on enough DUV machines from western machine-maker ASML to support their next three years of expansion plans. This is despite the push—not just from the Chinese government but also from companies such as Huawei, as the FT also reports—to back domestic production and eliminate foreign tech from China. Domestic alternatives are still said to be a few years behind ASML machines' productivity levels. This latest price increase for Intel CPUs looks set to take effect from October 5, this year. A number of lower-core product lines will also be nearing end-of-life, according to supply chain sources that spoke to DigiTimes . It remains unclear which processors will be impacted in either case. This follows last month's report of a desktop CPU sales slump for both Intel and AMD . The most recent Intel price increases affecting PC gamers were for the Core Ultra 7 270K Plus and the Core 5 250K Plus . Part of the continuing upward trend can be blamed on increasing prices for PCBs, which is also having a knock-on effect on motherboard prices . The memory supply crisis also doesn't help. But additionally, sources say Intel CEO Chen Liwu is looking into the CPU segment of the business anyway, reviewing pricing and profit. Speaking of restructuring, though, DigiTimes' sources also claim that there will be further layoffs at Intel. In 2024, its games Jusant and Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden sold "well below expectations" , causing it to pause development of two further games. Then, in 2025, it laid off several employees after Lost Records didn't quite make up the difference. Based on this financial update (thanks, GamesIndustry.biz ), its third-person adventure game Aphelion didn't pull things back from the brink, either. The developer reported a 56% decrease in operating revenue year-on-year, "amid systemic pressures in the video game industry, characterized by highly selective financing." items.summary: High NA EUV and even 12-inch photomasks.
items.body: Samsung is set to use ASML's latest high NA EUV machines for "volume manufacturing" by 2028, and TSMC is set to do the same from 2030, according to the world's sole EUV machine maker (via Bloomberg ). 'High NA EUV' stands for "high numerical aperture extreme ultraviolet", and refers to the tippity top-end chipmaking technology found in ASML's most advanced machines. The technology has been in active use by Intel and SK hynix for a short while . It allows for faster production and higher yields thanks to how it simplifies the chipmaking process, removing some production steps. It also produces more dense wafers. According to Bloomberg, ASML will also be working with Samsung, TSMC, Nvidia, and Apple to move from 6-inch photomasks to 12-inch ones, though I can only see official ASML announcements for the first three . These are the designs the EUV optics shine through to stencil chip designs onto wafers, and upping the mask to 12 inches will mean more of a wafer can be covered with each EUV shot, meaning fewer shots need to be fixed together and, well, performed at all, meaning cheaper and more efficient production. items.title: Valve appears to implementing a reservation system for the Steam Frame, suggesting it expects demand will outstrip supply at launch
items.summary: Closer than you think.
items.body: A release date for the Steam Frame has not yet been officially announced. However, data mining by VR leaker Brad Lynch has unearthed a reservation system in Valve's back-end, suggesting the hardware may not be far off. Lynch shared a look at the definitely not yet live reservation system on X . "Expect nothing. It isn’t ready," he posted, accompanied by a screenshot of a lottery drawing notification email claiming the draw results would be revealed on the placeholder date of 31 December, 1969. Obviously, Valve aren't time travellers, and this date was likely chosen to avoid any part of this system going live before it's meant to. Lynch wrote that the reservation system "is already up in Steam's backend for these two SKUs" in an earlier post , but shared no further hardware details. The data miner then added, "Before you ask: No. You can’t do anything with this information to beat the lottery system." A reservation system isn't all that surprising, as Valve had these in place for both the Steam Machine and the new Steam Controller . items.body: نجم برشلونة السابق يفجرها لم يعتزل جيرارد بيكيه إثارة الجدل باعتزاله كرة القدم، فمدافع برشلونة السابق، المعروف بعشقه لوسائل التواصل الاجتماعي، عاد ليضع نفسه في قلب العاصفة مرة أخرى، وهذه المرة برد ناري على أحد مستخدمي تيك توك، فتح فيه دفاتر تاريخية قديمة يرى أنها تدين غريمه الأزلي ريال مدريد. "لا نفوز إلا بالكرة الجميلة" بدأت القصة بتعليق استفزازي من أحد المستخدمين لمواقع التواصل كتب فيه: "لا يوجد سوى طريقة واحدة لفوز برشلونة، ونحن نعلم ذلك جيداً"، في إشارة مبطنة إلى التحكيم. ولم يتردد بيكيه في الرد بفيديو مباشر، وقال بلهجة حادة: "نعم، لا يوجد سوى طريقة واحدة لفوز برشلونة، وهي تقديم كرة قدم رائعة. لهذا السبب نحن مشهورون".  وأضاف: "لقد فزنا بالعديد من الدوريات، والعديد من ألقاب دوري أبطال أوروبا، والعديد من الثلاثيات بفضل تقديمنا كرة قدم رائعة.. أنتم دائماً ما تثيرون قضية الحكام، وإذا أردتم، فسأذكركم". فتح الدفاتر القديمة وانتقل بيكيه من الدفاع إلى الهجوم، مستعرضاً ما يعتبره أخطاء تاريخية صبت في مصلحة ريال مدريد في أهم البطولات. وقال: "سأذكركم بنهائي دوري أبطال أوروبا ضد يوفنتوس، وهدف مياتوفيتش الذي كان غير قانوني". وتابع: "أو في إحدى المباراتين النهائيتين ضد أتلتيكو مدريد، كان هدف سيرجيو راموس تسللاً، وكان أيضاً غير قانوني". وختم بيكيه رسالته بالجملة التي ستشعل مواقع التواصل …

items.body: Final Fantasy 7's remake trilogy has, at the very least, given us a trio of pretty solid RPGs—I had a great time with the first, and I'm soon to buckle up and finally give Rebirth a go. But I can't help but wonder, quietly, whether or not Final Fantasy has fallen into the same 'fear of new IP trap' as other games. That's not to say that the FF series isn't getting new games. Final Fantasy 16 came out in 2023 and snagged a solid 79 from us in our Final Fantasy 16 review . And yet, a small part of me wonders what new and exciting games we might've gotten if Square Enix had devoted the Remake team to making new final fantasies, rather than spending three entire big-budget titles and over half a decade rehashing a classic. And yet, Square seems reluctant to release its grip over the FF7 cast. That's per a PAX West panel (thanks, GamesRadar+ ) wherein director Naoki Hamaguchi said (via translator): "We want to make this a work that creates new fans 20 or even 30 years from now," a game that can "move beyond being a classic of the past and shape it into an IP with an ever-evolving future." And listen, I don't want to be a grumpy old git about this, but… that's just what Final Fantasy is…

Lots of people on the internet, on Twitter and in various forums like Reddit, confessed to having become addicted to it. Cookie Clicker did have an antecedent in Ian Bogost's Cow Clicker, which was a very deliberate satire . But Cookie Clicker wasn't presented as satire. It has the same simple, awe-inspiring majesty as Mass Effect's take on the concept, and you can explore it like an isometric videogame: Left click and drag to pan around, right click to rotate the camera, mouse wheel to zoom in and out. You can click on notable planets or regions to get little lore entries, or pull 'em up by name in the index to snap straight there on the map. Back in 2021, modder Jayveer showed off a map ported from Metal Gear Arcade into Metal Gear Online 2 , the multiplayer accompaniment to MGS4, but to my knowledge, TriggerHappy's is the first demonstration of a custom singleplayer map in MGS4. items.title: 'There is absolutely no generative AI in Space Marine 3' promises Saber Interactive executive
items.summary: The Machine Spirits lie silent.
items.body: In a Gamescom interview with IGN , Saber CCO and former id Software dev Tim Willits said that the company's upcoming Space Marine follow-up is not using generative AI in its development. The studio has otherwise been embracing the technology, which was at the heart of the recent Rideshare Stimulator controversy . "There is absolutely no generative AI in Space Marine 3 or Hellraiser or Stuntman or Turok or Jurassic Park, or [ Saber's John Wick game ]," Willits told IGN. "But like we said, we're going to experiment with it. Try it out in Rideshare, see if it works. See if people like it. If they don't like it, we're like, 'All right.'" It seems that Saber is far more circumspect about using generative AI in its big ticket games, especially when there are license holders like Lionsgate or Paramount to consider. Warhammer 40K owner Games Workshop, for its part, is enforcing strict internal rules against genAI use in any of its products or advertising, a crowd-pleasing stance that contrasts with rival tabletop giant Wizards of the Coast's willingness to play footsie with AI usage. I have half a dozen VGM playlists dedicated to stuff like the gym, relaxing, and locking in at work. I've formed lifelong memories with friends as we've filled karaoke rooms with the sound of all kinds of Final Fantasy 14 tracks, where our so-called tastes in "regular" music might misalign; we're instead united by our mutual love and attachment to the songs we hear in a game. It's tempting to say that these games ought to just stay under wraps until they're done and relatively bug-free—but at Gamescom 2026, GSC Game World CEO and head of game direction Ievgen Grygorovych told PC Gamer's Joshua Wolens that deciding when to release is a more complex consideration than you might think. As for why the studio didn't just wait to release the game until it was in the state it is now, Grygorovych cited both creative and financial reasons. "To make something better, you need to receive feedback, and this feedback should be fresh. From a business perspective, it's also impossible, because it's very expensive to do two years of additional work … in most cases, it's unrealistic." GSC Game World has more legitimate reasons than most to release an unfinished game. items.body: Listen, I'll be the first to admit that I'm a little biased towards parry-based action games . Sekiro will forever be my favourite FromSoftware game because of just how excellently it captured the back-and-forth feeling of swordplay, not only with its timed deflection mechanic, but its mandate to have you keep the pressure on. But I appreciate that, for some, parry fatigue might be setting in. My fellow writer Mollie Taylor's sick of it , for instance—and I do understand. I think there are some games which use it as a bit of a crutch, and even the ones that don't can wear out their welcome. Take Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, for instance. I liked it, but I wouldn't want every turn-based RPG I play to have a timed block in it. Still, it's fun to have the occasional one where stats can be overcome with deft enough bumper hands. But to paint every parry-based system with the same brush seems short-sighted to me, because this deceptively simple mechanic has a ton of juice still left inside it: no other game proves this more than Onimusha: Way of the Sword, which, as far as I'm concerned, has broken new ground in terms of what parries can do. items.summary: Playing the demo for Deficit was far from a net loss.
items.body: Immersive sims like Deus Ex and Dishonored are among the hardest kinds of games to make, so I always try to be supportive when an indie developer takes on the absurd challenge of creating one. Yet while there have been some good examples in recent years like Skin Deep and New Blood's early access Thief-like Gloomwood , a lot of the experiments in indie imsim design have been simply too janky for me to enjoy. Part of the problem is I'm a highly tactile player, and my primary concern when playing any game is whether it feels good beneath the fingers. If a game falls at that initial hurdle, then it's likely (though not inevitable) that I'll drop it pretty quickly. Fortunately, I had the opposite experience with Deficit , an indie imsim with such a strong sense of physicality that I kept playing the demo despite some clear issues. items.title: Confession time: Alright, come clean—how tidy are your bags in your MMOs?
items.summary: Mine? Mine are an utter mess.
items.body: Terminally Online (Image credit: Future) This is Terminally Online : PC Gamer's very own MMO column. Every other week, I'll be sharing my thoughts on the genre, interviewing fellow MMO-heads like me, taking a deep-dive into mechanics we've all taken for granted, and, occasionally, bringing in guest writers to talk about their MMO of choice. Ah, the MMO inventory. The delightful abstraction that means we don't need to actually think all that hard about where to store the hundreds of thousands of pelts, steaks, teeth, claws, trinkets, coins, crystals, and so-on that we accrue. Our bags are full of crap, it is tradition . On the one hand, I'm grateful for it. I'm out here to grind and run dungeons, not try to Jenga-stack a briefcase Resident Evil-style. items.title: This free lockpicking puzzler you can play in your browser is unexpectedly one of the most thrilling games I've encountered this year
items.summary: Lockpicks-11 is a fiendish delight.
items.body: I love lockpicking minigames, especially when representatively they're as far away from the act of lockpicking as possible. While I admire the elegance of Bethesda's bobby-pin/screwdriver system seen in Fallout 4 , I'm much more interested in the weirder solutions like Splinter Cell 's baffling pin-flicking system, or Gothic Remake 's absurdly elaborate sliding puzzle system. I love how developers have tried so many ways to represent the act of lockpicking, and that despite this nobody has 'solved' the problem of virtual lockpicking yet (though Bethesda has arguably come closest). Inevitably, then, I was drawn to the idea of a game that is all about lockpicking. But I never expected that it could be as imaginative and thrilling as Lockpicks-11 . An entry for Ludum Dare 57, Lockpicks-11 places you in the role of an unnamed thief in the middle of a heist. Yet rather than being a fully fledged burglary simulator like Thief, Lockpicks-11 distils the act of larceny to a linear sequence of locked doors. items.title: Gaming monitors are one of the only good things about PC hardware right now, but one niche feature is underloved
items.summary: Doubling your refresh rate with just a few clicks? Yes please.
items.body: The memory crisis may be in full swing, taking numerous PC components with it, but the value of gaming monitors is one of a few hardware things that has actually improved over the last few years. In fact, their price-to-quality ratio is kind of outrageous right now, with even relatively recent QD-OLED screens going for around $300 . As such, monitors are one of the few things I check over without rolling my eyes, and therefore, they're one of a handful of techie bits that actually excites me. But that doesn't mean even they can't improve; when I chatted to gaming monitor brand AOC a few months ago, even its designers are aware the software isn't up to snuff. I've been testing out the Koorui G2741L, a dual mode 4K/1080p monitor, over the last few weeks, and all I can think is 'gosh, why aren't more companies doing dual mode,' and 'why aren't more companies doing dual mode better ?' The central argument for dual mode makes so much sense to me. When you want your games to look pretty, you swap to 4K at a lower refresh rate, and when you want something snappy and competitive, you drop it to 1080p with a much higher refresh rate.
